name: Verisk Analytics, Inc.
executive_summary: Verisk Analytics is a high-quality, insurance-focused data and analytics franchise with durable subscription economics, strong free cash flow, and deep workflow integration across underwriting and claims. The quantitative screen rates VRSK as a buy (four models passed across cheapness, dividend, GARP and risk families; composite score 61%), supported by a low PEGY (0.27), earnings quality and dividend growth signals at a P/E near 29x. The valuation hook is a reset after a prolonged share-price decline: the market is pricing slower growth and AI disruption risk against a business still compounding revenue at mid-single digits with EBITDA margins above 55%. The central debate is whether Verisk’s proprietary datasets and regulatory moat offset rising leverage from aggressive buybacks, litigation overhangs, and the failed AccuLynx acquisition.
investment_thesis: For a value investor, VRSK offers a rare combination of recurring revenue, pricing power and capital return at a screen-validated entry point. The screen passes Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula and Earnings Quality — signalling that earnings are cash-backed, dividends are growing, and growth-adjusted valuation is attractive relative to quality. Business fundamentals align with those signals: the FY2025 10-K describes subscription/pre-paid contracts representing over 80% of revenue, with approximately 70% of revenue from US P&C primary insurers and all top-100 P&C clients among customers; Q1 2026 interim filings show 84% of insurance revenue from hosted subscriptions. Operating leverage remains intact — Q1 2026 revenue rose 3.9% to $782.6m while operating income grew 6.7% to $352.2m and EBITDA margin expanded to 55.7% ($436.0m). Negative reported book value (screen P/B −22.6) reflects cumulative treasury stock from buybacks rather than impaired assets; goodwill of $1,878m at 31 December 2025 (Q1 2026 10-Q) sits against retained earnings of $7,811m. Capital allocation is shareholder-friendly: quarterly dividend raised to $0.50 per share in Q1 2026, and the board authorised a $2.5bn repurchase programme after a $1.5bn accelerated share repurchase in February 2026. Yahoo-sourced FY2025 free cash flow of $1,192m (operating cash flow $1,436m less capex $244m) supports the screen’s FCF yield case; this is consistent with the cash-generative profile evident in interim filings.

Interim figures are from SEC 10-Q body extracts.

FY2023 net income was depressed by a $154m discontinued-operations loss (Energy sale completed February 2023, per FY2025 10-K business description). FY2025 net income of $908m (Yahoo) compares with $951m in FY2024, partly reflecting higher interest expense ($171m vs $125m) as debt expanded.

**Interim momentum (primary filings)**

*Q1 2026 (10-Q, filed 29 April 2026):* Revenue $782.6m (+3.9% YoY); operating income $352.2m (+6.7%); net income $234.2m (+0.8%); diluted EPS $1.73 (+4.8%); EBITDA $436.0m, margin 55.7%. Underwriting revenue $552.1m (+3.8%); claims $230.5m (+4.3%). Adjusted for recent acquisitions/disposition (Simplitium, SuranceBay, Verisk Marketing Solutions sale), organic insurance revenue grew approximately 5.5%. Operating cash flow $390.4m (vs $444.7m prior year, reflecting working-capital timing); capex $64.0m.

*Q3 2025 (10-Q, filed 29 October 2025):* Q3 revenue $768.3m (+5.9% YoY); nine-month revenue $2,294m (+6.9% YoY). Q3 operating income $345.9m (+11.0% YoY); nine-month operating income $1,030m (+9.9% YoY). Nine-month net income $711m.

*Balance sheet and leverage (Q1 2026 10-Q):* Cash fell to $525m from $2,178m at year-end 2025 following the $1.5bn ASR and debt activity; total debt $4,476m (31 March 2026) vs $4,737m (31 December 2025). Stockholders’ equity turned to a deficit of $(1,167)m due to treasury stock of $(12,132)m. Senior notes aggregate $4,250m; company states compliance with financial covenants (interest coverage ≥3.0x; funded debt leverage ≤3.75x). February 2026 issuance of $500m 4.450% 2031 notes and $500m 5.125% 2036 notes; January 2026 redemption of $1,500m AccuLynx-related notes at 101% special mandatory redemption price (FY2025 loss on extinguishment $33.9m per Q1 2026 10-Q Note 7).

*FY2025 qualitative (10-K body):* Verisk Marketing Solutions sold 31 December 2025 for $80.0m net cash. No going-concern language identified in available extracts. Pension and postretirement plans are frozen; Q1 2026 net periodic pension benefit of $(1.9)m.

risks_and_flags:
**Customer and cyclical concentration.** The FY2025 10-K states approximately 70% of revenue derives from US P&C primary insurers, with certain invoices linked to industry premium volumes — cyclical softness in P&C pricing or cat-loss years could dampen growth.

**Leverage and capital structure.** Aggressive buybacks ($624m FY2025 per Yahoo; $1.5bn ASR plus open-market purchases in Q1 2026 per 10-Q) have been debt-funded, lifting total debt toward $4.5bn and producing negative tangible book. Q1 2026 interest expense rose 19% YoY to $43.2m. Credit agreements require interest coverage ≥3.0x and leverage ≤3.75x — no default disclosed, but reduced flexibility if earnings weaken.

**Litigation and contingencies (Q1 2026 10-Q Note 13).** Multiple matters with unquantifiable loss ranges: telematics/class-action driving-data litigation (MDL consolidated in Georgia); JPMorgan Chase trade-secrets suit (discovery ongoing); AccuLynx merger termination dispute (Delaware Chancery trial scheduled June 2026 — Verisk filed declaratory judgment; counterclaims for breach); Daniel’s Law data-privacy claims (111 cases, MCL application pending). Company states it cannot reasonably estimate ultimate resolution. Data Driven Safety commercial litigation settled and dismissed February 2026.

**Strategic/M&A execution.** AccuLynx acquisition terminated 26 December 2025 after $1.5bn note issuance; special mandatory redemption cost a 1% premium plus accelerated amortisation. Signals discipline in walking away but creates legal and financing friction.

**Competitive and technology.** FY2025 10-K risk factors highlight AI-driven competitors, free public data alternatives, and long selling cycles. News flow repeatedly flags AI as both opportunity and threat to Verisk’s data-licensing model.

**Regulatory.** Licensed statistical agent in all US states; regulatory filing obligations and antitrust scrutiny of advisory-organisation activities remain structural compliance burdens.

**Governance.** Routine CFO 10b5-1 sale of 400 shares (July 2025) — immaterial; no broader governance red flags in sources.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is substantial, though much is price-action and earnings-preview commentary rather than deep strategy reporting.

**M&A and capital allocation**
- AccuLynx acquisition agreement signed July 2025; terminated 26 December 2025 — litigation ongoing (*How The Verisk Analytics (VRSK) Narrative Is Shifting On Growth, AI Risk And Valuation*, 15 May 2025; Q1 2026 10-Q Note 13).
- $1.5bn accelerated share repurchase and $2.5bn authorisation increase (February 2026, per Q1 2026 10-Q).
- Verisk Marketing Solutions divestiture completed 31 December 2025 (FY2025 10-K).

**Product and strategy**
- KatRisk catastrophe-modelling integration and upgraded hurricane analytics (*Here's Why Verisk's Stock Is a Great Pick for Investors Now*, 2 July 2026).
- CargoNet cargo-theft data integration with Trucker Path (*Does Verisk (VRSK) Index Shuffle Recast Its Role in Data-Driven Risk Management Portfolios?*, 3 July 2026).

**Market and sentiment**
- Jefferies upgrade, price target raised to $235 (*VRSK Upgraded by Jefferies -- Price Target Raised to $235*, 23 July 2026).
- Counter-narrative on weakness: *2 Reasons to Avoid VRSK and 1 Stock to Buy Instead* (14 July 2026) citing ~13.6% six-month decline; *Verisk Analytics (VRSK) Stock After 43% Slide Is The Valuation Reset Enough* (21 June 2026).
- Russell index rebalancing removed VRSK from growth benchmarks, added to Russell 1000 Dynamic (3 July 2026).
- Q2 2026 earnings scheduled 29 July 2026 (*Verisk will report Q2 results July 29 before the market opens*, 8 July 2026).

**Management changes:** No CEO or CFO transitions reported in the manifest; director retainer share grants only (July 2026).
research_rationale: Interim SEC filings confirm durable subscription growth, margin expansion and strong cash generation that support the quantitative buy signal, but elevated leverage, unresolved litigation and missing annual statement extracts in the filing pack prevent full conviction without further verification.
